title: MCP
description: Plug Claude into GitHub, databases, browsers and more with the Model Context Protocol.

lessons.title: What Is MCP?
lessons.description: Servers that give Claude new tools

theory.title: A universal plug for tools
theory.body:
**MCP** stands for **Model Context Protocol**: an open standard for connecting AI tools like Claude Code to external systems and data.

An **MCP server** exposes tools Claude can call. Connect the GitHub server and Claude can read issues and open PRs. Connect a database server and it can query your tables. Connect Playwright and it can drive a real browser.

Kip's take: MCP is like bolting new limbs onto the shell. Same crab, many more claws.
theory.code:
# Tools from a server show up with names like
mcp__github__list_issues
mcp__db__query

theory.title: Local vs remote servers
theory.body:
Servers come in two main flavors.

**stdio** servers run as a local process on your machine, started by a command such as `npx ...`.

**HTTP** servers live at a URL and are the recommended option for remote services. The older **SSE** transport is deprecated.

Only add servers you trust: a server that fetches outside content can expose Claude to **prompt injection**.

exercises.explanation: MCP is the Model Context Protocol, an open standard for connecting Claude to external tools and data.

exercises.prompt: What does connecting an MCP server give Claude?
options: New tools and data sources from an external system
exercises.explanation: An MCP server exposes tools (and sometimes resources) that Claude can call to reach an outside system.

exercises.prompt: Match each MCP server to what it lets Claude do.
exercises.explanation: Each server plugs Claude into one external system and exposes that system's actions as tools.

exercises.code:
MCP stands for Model ___ Protocol.
Local servers run as a process and talk over ___.
Remote servers are best connected over ___.
exercises.explanation: MCP is the Model Context Protocol; local servers use stdio and remote ones should use the HTTP transport.

exercises.prompt: You're connecting to a remote MCP server hosted at a URL. Which transport is recommended?
exercises.explanation: HTTP is the recommended transport for remote servers; SSE is deprecated and stdio is for local processes.

exercises.prompt: Tools from an MCP server named `github` appear to Claude with names like…
exercises.explanation: MCP tools are namespaced as mcp__<server>__<tool>, which is also the name you use in permission rules.

exercises.prompt: The GitHub MCP server is connected. You want help with issue #142 in acme/web.
options: Use the GitHub MCP server to read issue #142 in acme/web, summarize the bug, then propose a fix for src/cart.ts. Don't edit anything yet.
exercises.explanation: Naming the server, the repo, the issue and the file tells Claude exactly which tool to use and where to look.

exercises.prompt: Why should you only add MCP servers you trust?
options: Servers that fetch outside content can expose you to prompt injection
Claude can only connect to one server at a time
exercises.explanation: A server that pulls in external content could feed Claude malicious instructions, so vet what you connect.

exercises.scenario: A read-only Postgres MCP server named `db` is connected. Signups dropped last week and you want Claude to investigate without changing anything.
exercises.sample: Using the db MCP server (read-only), query daily signups for the last 14 days and show where the drop starts. Then read @src/signup/handler.ts and list changes that could explain it. Don't edit code yet; just report your findings.
exercises.explanation: Great MCP prompts name the server, the exact data to pull, and what Claude should (and shouldn't) do with it.

theory.title: claude mcp add
theory.body:
Add a **local stdio** server: put the server's launch command after `--`. Everything after `--` goes to the server untouched.

Add a **remote HTTP** server with `--transport http` followed by a name and a URL.

Pass secrets with `-e KEY=value` (or `--env`), and HTTP headers with `--header`.
theory.code:
# local stdio server
claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest

# remote HTTP server
claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp

# manage them
claude mcp list
claude mcp get notion
claude mcp remove notion

theory.title: Scopes and /mcp
theory.body:
`--scope` decides who sees a server:

**local** (default): just you, in this project.

**project**: written to `.mcp.json` at the repo root so the team shares it via git.

**user**: just you, in every project.

Inside a session, `/mcp` shows each server's status and handles **OAuth** login for remote servers. Kip checks it for the word `connected`.

exercises.prompt: Add a local stdio MCP server named playwright that runs `npx @playwright/mcp@latest`.
accepted: claude mcp add --transport stdio playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest
claude mcp add -t stdio playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest
exercises.explanation: For stdio servers, the name comes first and the server's launch command goes after `--`.

exercises.prompt: Add GitHub's remote MCP server over HTTP, named github, at https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/
accepted: claude mcp add --transport http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/
claude mcp add -t http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/
exercises.explanation: Remote servers use `--transport http` followed by a name and the server URL.

exercises.prompt: List every MCP server you've configured.
exercises.explanation: `claude mcp list` shows all configured servers.

exercises.prompt: Inside a session, check your servers' status and log in to one that needs OAuth.
exercises.explanation: `/mcp` shows server status and runs the OAuth flow for remote servers that need it.

exercises.prompt: Match each scope to who gets the server.
exercises.explanation: Local is the default, project shares through a checked-in `.mcp.json`, and user follows you everywhere.

exercises.prompt: Add Notion as a remote server and share it with your team.
exercises.code: claude mcp add ___ http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp ___ project
exercises.explanation: `--transport http` picks the remote transport and `--scope project` writes it to `.mcp.json` for the team.

exercises.prompt: Complete this project-scoped config file at the repo root.
exercises.explanation: `.mcp.json` lists servers under `mcpServers`, and a remote one uses type `http` with a `url`.

exercises.prompt: In `claude mcp add myserver -- python server.py --port 8080`, what does the `--` do?
options: Comments out the rest of the line
Separates Claude's own options from the server's command and args
Runs the server in the background
exercises.explanation: Everything after `--` is passed to the server untouched, so `--port 8080` goes to server.py, not to Claude.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps for connecting a remote server that uses OAuth in order.
steps: Run claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
Run /mcp and select the notion server
Finish the OAuth login in your browser
Confirm it shows connected, then ask Claude to use it
exercises.explanation: Add the server from your shell, then authenticate and verify it inside a session with `/mcp`.

exercises.prompt: Remove the MCP server named notion.
exercises.explanation: `claude mcp remove <name>` deletes a server's config (and stored OAuth tokens for remote servers).

mission.title: Plug In a Server
mission.intro: Time to give Kip a new claw. Connect a real MCP server and make Claude use one of its tools.
checklist: Add a trusted server, e.g. claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest
Run claude mcp list to confirm it's configured
Start claude and run /mcp; make sure the server shows connected
Ask Claude to use one of its tools (e.g. open your local dev site and describe the page)
Run claude mcp get <name> to inspect its config
mission.explanation: Connecting a server and calling its tools is the core MCP loop you'll reuse for GitHub, databases and more.

cheatsheet.description: Model Context Protocol: open standard connecting Claude to external tools and data.
Add a local stdio server; its launch command goes after --.
Add a remote HTTP server (recommended for remote).
Who gets the server; local is the default.
Pass an environment variable to the server (also --env).
Check server status and authenticate with OAuth.
Project-scoped servers at the repo root, shared via git.
How MCP tool names appear in permissions and rules.
